text: Apple reported quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, with Services revenue reaching an all-time high.
iPhone revenue increased 3% year over year despite a challenging macroeconomic environment in Greater China.
The Company's business depends on a small number of contract manufacturers concentrated in Asia, and any disruption to those relationships could materially affect production.
Apple faces increasing regulatory scrutiny in the European Union and other jurisdictions regarding its App Store policies.
Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 22% year over year, led by continued strong demand for Azure and other cloud services.
Productivity and Business Processes segment revenue increased, driven by growth in Microsoft 365 Commercial products.
Intense competition in cloud infrastructure and AI services could pressure Microsoft's pricing and market share over time.
Cybersecurity incidents, including sophisticated nation-state attacks, pose an ongoing risk to Microsoft's products and customer trust.
Alphabet's advertising revenue increased, with particular strength in YouTube ads and Google Search.
Google Cloud revenue grew and the segment reported an operating profit for a second consecutive quarter.
Alphabet faces ongoing antitrust litigation in the United States and European Union related to its search and advertising businesses.
Changes to browser and platform privacy policies could reduce the effectiveness of Alphabet's advertising products.
